title: Sanctions screening coverage and timing across parties and the grant lifecycle
status_rationale: CNV-GRT-006 (adopted convergence clause, owner-ratified) requires screening of donors, advisors, successors, grantees and payors at onboarding, automatic delta screening on list updates, and screening before each grant release against the current list version, with dispatch fenced atomically at the irreversible step. UNB-EXT-004 requires screening against legally applicable lists with source freshness and warns against equating name similarity with a match. UNB-RULE-014 blocks grant execution while sanctions status is unresolved. Not implemented. Screening of grantee principals and ownership (50 percent rule) is not specified in located requirements.
target_answer: Donors, advisors, successors, grantees and payors are screened at onboarding, re-screened automatically whenever a list changes, and screened again immediately before each irreversible release; a match found during release prevents transmission because the check and the dispatch are one atomic step. Lists include the SDN list and OFAC consolidated non-SDN lists, with other lists (UN, EU, UK) available by sponsor policy. Entity screening covers known owners and principals of grantee organizations where data is available, and the sponsor policy records how the 50 percent rule is addressed. Coverage is complete by construction: no party can be attached to a fund or grant without a screening record.
intended_practice: Implement per CNV-GRT-006 and CNV-ARC-003; extend to grantee principals and ownership data.
customer_statement: Echelon's adopted design screens donors, advisors, successors, grantees and payors at onboarding, on every list update and immediately before each grant release, and blocks release when a potential match is unresolved. Not yet implemented.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: sponsor compliance officer for policy; Unbound product owner for enforcement)
residual_risks: Ownership data for grantee organizations is often unavailable, limiting 50 percent rule coverage.
open_questions: Which list data provider will be used, and does it include OFAC consolidated non-SDN lists and ownership data?

title: Screening list freshness and fail-closed behavior
status_rationale: CNV-GRT-006 requires every release screening to record list version and fetch time, to fail closed when the list is older than a basis-tagged bound or the screening service is unavailable, and to distribute list updates as versioned inter-cell messages covered by the dispatch fence. Not implemented; the freshness bound value is not yet set.
target_answer: Echelon ingests official list updates from OFAC (and other configured sources) within a defined bound, verifies integrity of the downloaded data, versions each list snapshot, and triggers delta re-screening of all parties. Every screening records list version and fetch time. If the list is older than the bound or screening is unavailable, releases stop rather than proceed unscreened. Freshness lag is monitored and alerted.
intended_practice: Set the freshness bound with the sponsor compliance officer and implement per CNV-GRT-006.
customer_statement: Echelon's design records the list version used for every screening and stops grant releases if the sanctions list is stale or screening is unavailable. Not yet implemented.
open_questions: What freshness bound will be set, and on what basis (CNV-GRT-006 requires it to be basis-tagged)?

title: Name matching method, threshold tuning, effectiveness testing and subgroup fairness
status_rationale: CNV-GRT-006 requires the matcher to meet a recall target approved by the sponsor compliance officer on a versioned perturbation suite (exact, case and punctuation, dropped character, token reorder, legal suffix, listed names on otherwise clean identifiers) before release and after every matcher or threshold change; no listed name attached to a clean identifier may pass straight through; false-alert rates must be measured by name subgroup including Arabic-origin or Islamic tokens at every change and at least quarterly. It records that the reference matcher in report 14 does not meet this and must not be used in production. Not implemented.
target_answer: The matching method (normalization, transliteration, token, phonetic and edit-distance components, secondary identifiers) is documented. Thresholds are approved by the sponsor compliance officer from measured recall on the versioned perturbation suite and false-alert rates by subgroup, and are change-controlled: any change re-runs the suite and blocks release if recall falls below target. Secondary identifiers (date of birth, address, country, EIN) are used to support disposition, not to suppress alerts automatically. AI and machine learning do not close alerts; if used at all they only prioritize review queues and are evaluated like any matcher change.
current_practice: Not established. A reference matcher exists in Unbound research materials (report 14) and is recorded as not meeting the recall requirement.
intended_practice: Select or build a matcher that meets the perturbation suite, then implement the change gate and subgroup reporting.
customer_statement: Echelon's design requires its sanctions name matching to meet a compliance-approved recall target on a published perturbation test suite, retested on every change, with false-alert rates measured by name subgroup. No production matcher exists yet.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: sponsor compliance officer approves thresholds; Unbound product owner maintains matcher)
residual_risks: Perturbation suites cannot cover every transliteration variant; some true matches may still be missed.

challenge.customer_intent: Sponsors and banks want assurance that screening catches listed parties without drowning staff in false alerts or burdening donors and grantees with certain name origins.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A listed party passes screening because of a spelling variant, or legitimate grantees face repeated holds because of their names.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional practice relies on a vendor's fuzzy score and a threshold set once; effectiveness is rarely measured, and vendors often do not disclose method or test results.
challenge.legally_required: OFAC does not mandate a matching method; it expects risk-based controls and testing (Framework 2019). Liability for dealing with a listed person is strict.
challenge.contractually_required: Banks may require evidence of screening tuning and testing from service providers.
challenge.historical_convention: Threshold tuning by trial and error and periodic model validation of the screening tool.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not eliminable; matching is inherently probabilistic. The pass-through of listed names on clean identifiers can be eliminated by rule.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release gate re-runs the perturbation suite on every matcher or threshold change.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-change recall and subgroup false-alert reports; quarterly at minimum.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Measured, gated recall against a versioned perturbation suite plus subgroup false-alert reporting, in place of an unvalidated vendor score threshold.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Suite, results and thresholds can be reviewed by sponsor compliance, auditors and examiners.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If the perturbation suite is unrepresentative of real list entries and name variants, measured recall overstates real recall.
challenge.alternative_risks: Optimizing to the suite can overfit; the suite must grow from real misses and list changes.
supporting_arguments: Subgroup reporting addresses fairness concerns explicitly.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely among compliance professionals; it exceeds common vendor practice. Some banks will still require their own model validation.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Requires ongoing compliance involvement to approve thresholds.
Real-world recall is still unknown without production data.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Alert disposition, blocking and rejecting, and OFAC reporting
status_rationale: CNV-GRT-006 requires confirmed matches to resolve to Block, Reject or Proceed (license or exemption), never automatically to Blocked; block or reject actions to produce 31 CFR 501.603 and 501.604 report data due within 10 business days; blocked property to enter the annual report; potential matches at release to open a disposition task with a sponsor-set due date and escalation, never auto-release; dispositions to record the facts compared and never cite a score as the reason; false-positive dispositions reusable within the deciding sponsor until defined expiry events; donor-facing status to use a neutral catalog without list names or scores. UNB-RCN-REG-003 requires recording blocked property and preventing movement. CNV-GRT-012 requires neutral decline wording. NoAiClearance (EDF) and UNB-AGT-002 bar AI from clearing alerts. Not implemented.
target_answer: Potential matches open a disposition task assigned to a qualified sponsor reviewer with a due date and escalation to the compliance officer. Only an authorized human disposes of an alert; AI may assemble evidence but cannot clear. The disposition records the specific facts compared and the reviewer's reasoning; scores are not reasons. True matches resolve to Block, Reject or Proceed under a license, generate report data for filing within 10 business days, and blocked property is held in place and included in the annual report. Prior false-positive dispositions are reused only within the same sponsor and expire on subject or list change, new match, 12 months or reviewer authority revocation. A risk-stratified sample of dispositions receives second-level review. Donors see neutral status only.
intended_practice: Implement per CNV-GRT-006, UNB-RCN-REG-003 and CNV-GRT-012.
customer_statement: Echelon's adopted design requires every potential sanctions match to be disposed of by an authorized human with recorded reasoning, supports blocking, rejecting and OFAC report preparation, and never lets AI clear an alert. Not yet implemented.
residual_risks: Disposition quality depends on reviewer skill; the second-level sample is the check.

title: Sanctions and AML recordkeeping
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-004 requires transaction-level records, screening results, dispositions and license reliance records retained 10 years after the transaction; blocked property records while blocked plus 10 years; legal holds override disposition; and in release 1 a 10-year floor for all transaction-level financial and grant records. SOC2-006 requires append-only records with integrity verification. Not implemented.
target_answer: Screening results (with list version and fetch time), alerts, dispositions, license reliance records, blocked and rejected transaction records and reports are retained at least for the periods in CNV-PLT-004, which meet or exceed the OFAC recordkeeping period, in append-only, hash-verified storage. A complete screening history for any party or transaction can be produced for an examiner within a defined time. Retention survives tenant offboarding as required and legal holds override deletion.
customer_statement: Echelon's design retains sanctions screening results, dispositions and related transaction records for at least 10 years in tamper-evident storage, producible for examiners. Not yet implemented.
open_questions: Confirm the current OFAC recordkeeping period in 31 CFR 501.601 as of the answer date.

title: Support for BSA/AML program obligations of bank and broker-dealer sponsors and partners
status_rationale: RR-UNB-PART-007-r1 and UNB-RCN-ENT-014 separate sanctions screening, identity proofing, any customer identification or AML program (enabled only when counsel records that it applies, by law or by contract with a custodian or payment provider) and source-of-funds checks, each with an authority type and owner. CNV-PLT-003 requires risk-based identity proofing. UNB-CHAR-028 and UNB-GRANT-029 require detection of suspicious patterns as signals, not guilt. TVR-CMP-003 notes BSA scope depends on operating model. Whether any BSA program obligation applies to Echelon, to a given sponsor or only to its bank or broker-dealer partners requires counsel determination; Echelon's design (CNV-LEG-001) avoids holding or moving funds.
target_answer: Echelon does not itself operate as a BSA financial institution and says so only after counsel confirms it. For sponsors affiliated with or partnered with banks or broker-dealers that must run AML programs, Unbound supports their programs: configurable identity verification and beneficial ownership collection, risk-based monitoring rules that surface unusual patterns (structuring of contributions, rapid pass-through of contributions to grants, unusual grant patterns) as cases for the sponsor's or partner's investigators, case export for SAR decisions made by the responsible institution, strict confidentiality of any SAR-related information with access restricted to named roles, and data and documentation for independent AML testing and examinations. Echelon personnel and AI agents never decide whether to file a SAR.
intended_practice: Obtain counsel determination per RR-UNB-PART-007-r1 for each operating model; build the applicability register UNB-RCN-ENT-014.
customer_statement: Echelon's design does not hold or move funds and is not intended to make Echelon a BSA financial institution; counsel has not yet confirmed this. Echelon plans to support sponsors' and partners' AML programs with identity verification, monitoring signals and case data, while SAR decisions stay with the responsible institution.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon counsel for applicability; sponsor or partner BSA officer for program decisions)
open_questions: The FinCEN investment adviser AML rule now takes effect January 1, 2028 (SRC-FINCEN-IA-AML-RULE-2024); will it change any target customer's expectations of Unbound before or after that date?
Which target sponsors operate under bank or broker-dealer AML programs that would flow requirements to Unbound?

challenge.customer_intent: Bank and broker-dealer affiliated sponsors need vendors to support their AML programs without creating gaps or tipping-off risks.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Money laundering or terrorist financing through DAF contributions and grants goes undetected, or a SAR is disclosed.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Rule-based transaction monitoring generates high false-positive volumes; its effectiveness in the charitable context is not well documented, and DAF sponsors that are not BSA financial institutions often have no monitoring at all.
challenge.legally_required: BSA AML program rules bind banks (31 CFR 1020.210) and broker-dealers (31 CFR 1023.210), not charities or software vendors as such. Obligations reach Echelon only by contract or if Echelon's activity made it a financial institution, which its design avoids.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank and broker-dealer partners commonly flow AML support duties to service providers.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendors expected to run monitoring scenarios like banks.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Funds never pass through Echelon (CNV-LEG-001), removing Echelon from the money flow; the responsible institution keeps its program.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Deterministic monitoring rules with versioned thresholds generate cases.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Signals and evidence delivered to the responsible institution's investigators with clear ownership, instead of Echelon operating an AML program it is not obligated to run.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Applicability register, rule definitions and case logs are reviewable.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If counsel finds a BSA obligation applies to Echelon in some operating model, a full program is required.
challenge.alternative_risks: Ownership confusion between sponsor, partner and Echelon could leave alerts uninvestigated.
supporting_arguments: Keeps legal judgments with the obligated institution.
Avoids Echelon becoming a de facto financial institution.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; some partners may expect the vendor to operate monitoring end to end.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Partners may see it as shifting work back to them.
Small sponsors without a BSA function will receive signals they cannot act on.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Charity-specific diligence: Treasury guidelines, foreign grants, prohibited benefits and grant fraud red flags
status_rationale: CNV-GRT-003 requires charity status checks at approval and release against IRS data; CNV-GRT-007 requires versioned reliance on OFAC general licenses and risk-based FCPA diligence for foreign grants; CNV-GRT-008 governs intermediaries and foreign paths and forbids naming specific foreign organizations to intermediaries; CNV-GRT-009 forbids payments benefiting donors, advisors, family or 35 percent controlled entities; CNV-GRT-011 routes risk signals (donor benefit, supporting organizations, intermediaries with country preference, equivalency-based foreign recipients, unusual size or restrictions) to Tier 2 review; UNB-CHAR-028 detects impersonation and suspicious bank changes; UNB-GRANT-029 detects split or repeated grants; UNB-GRANT-041 allows international grants only through separately approved frameworks; CNV-PLT-011 notifies prior channels of contact changes. Not implemented.
target_answer: Grantee due diligence follows a risk-based approach informed by Treasury's voluntary anti-terrorist financing guidelines for charities: verify legal status and identity against IRS data at approval and release, screen the organization and known principals, and apply enhanced review to higher-risk grants. Foreign grants are disabled until a sponsor enables an approved framework (equivalency determination or expenditure responsibility, sanctions and license reliance, FCPA diligence, staged payments, use reporting). Red flags route to Tier 2 human review: donor or family benefit (IRC 4967), grants to related parties, intermediaries with stated country or program preferences (earmarking), split or rapid pass-through grants, newly changed bank details, impersonation indicators. Payee bank changes require verification through an independent channel and notice to the prior channel. AI may surface signals; only humans or sponsor-approved deterministic rules decide.
intended_practice: Implement per the cited convergence clauses.
customer_statement: Echelon's adopted design checks grantee status at approval and release, routes prohibited-benefit, earmarking, fraud and foreign-grant risk signals to human review, and keeps foreign grants disabled until a sponsor enables an approved diligence framework. Not yet implemented.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: sponsor grants and compliance officers)
residual_risks: Earmarking through intermediaries can be hidden in off-platform communications.
